contract.shape: 256 MiB sequential aligned stores followed by the target-appropriate completion fence
contract.working_set_reason: The range is larger than either qualification machine's last-level cache and measures the write-stream use case instead of an L1 register loop.
contract.ordering: Each process performs six samples per candidate and alternates HYLE-first and Highway-first internally.
contract.interpretation: Timing is a whole-range route input. Exact final code shape overrides a boundary-sized apparent winner; a repeatable instruction difference with a material workload effect remains actionable.

windows.finding: The first process landed just beyond the 5% material boundary, while two immediate reproductions were within 1.3%. The optimized loops are instruction-shape identical, so this is a tie and not a HYLE algorithm advantage.

macos.machine: MacBook Air Mac16,12 / Apple M4 / 16 GiB

disassembly.highway_loop: prfm pstl1strm, [x9]; str q0, [x9], #0x10; add; cmp; b.lo

macos.finding: Highway's per-vector AArch64 write-prefetch is materially harmful on the current Apple M4 workload. HYLE's plain store is 2.9x to 6.4x faster and matches the cached-store control, so the NEON difference is real rather than a code-placement tie.

route_conclusion: KEEP_HYLE globally for Stream: HYLE is exact-codegen tied on AVX2, source-equivalent on scalar/SSE4/AVX512/SVE/RVV, and materially better on the current NEON silicon. This avoids a target split without sacrificing a demonstrated winner.
